headline: Here is a detailed, step-by-step breakdown of the market analysis, technical indicators, sector trends, and individual stock setups covered in the source material:.
summary: Here is a detailed, step-by-step breakdown of the market analysis, technical indicators, sector trends, and individual stock setups covered in the source material:.

indexes.name: Index Summary
indexes.action: The NASDAQ Composite led Friday's advance with a 1.2% gain following the jobs report. The NASDAQ 100 (QQQ) gained 1%, the S&P 500 rose 0.7%, small caps (Russell 2000) added 0.8%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5%.

indexes.name: True Range Analysis
indexes.action: Although the NASDAQ's standard closing range ended near the lower third (~33%) of its daily span, evaluating the true range (factoring in the initial gap-up from the prior day's close) lifts the closing measure to roughly 66%. On the weekly chart, the NASDAQ remains positioned near the upper end of its range and holds near new high territory.

indexes.name: NASDAQ Levels
indexes.action: The index closed just above its previous marked high. Analysts highlight the September 22 high as a potential short-term magnet/resistance target to confirm full bullish control, while the lower gap-up zone serves as key downside support.

indexes.name: S&P 500 Levels
indexes.action: The S&P 500 successfully bounced off support at its 50-day moving average line. Upside resistance sits around the 7,800 level and the September 21–22 highs, whereas a break below the September 16 March low would signal heightened technical concern.

macro.title: 10-Year Treasury Yields
macro.text: Yields reversed higher after the jobs report was released. Despite this pressure from rising yields, the equities market demonstrated notable resilience by retaining the majority of its daily gains.

macro.title: Late-1990s Analog vs. Modern Earnings
macro.text: Analysts compared current market conditions to the late-1990s NASDAQ rally, where market breadth was narrow and concentrated in a small group of leaders. However, unlike the late-1990s—when companies were valued on "eyeballs rather than earnings"—today's technology and semiconductor leaders display phenomenal earnings growth rather than speculative valuations alone.

macro.title: Power Trend Activation
macro.text: The NASDAQ triggered a Power Trend, satisfying four strict criteria: 1. The 21-day moving average line has remained above the 50-day moving average line for more than five days. 2. The daily lows have held above the 21-day moving average line for ten consecutive days. 3. The 50-day moving average line is trending upwards. 4. The index recorded a positive trading session.

sectors.name: Semiconductors (SMH)
sectors.action: Gained nearly 4% for the week, breaking back above its 10-week moving average line. Leader NVIDIA reached new highs, with its market cap climbing past $5 trillion.

sectors.name: Bitcoin (IBIT)
sectors.action: Logged an intraday downside reversal off its session highs, but continues to hold constructively above its 200-day moving average line.

sectors.name: Steel & Metals (SLX)
sectors.action: Broke its immediate downtrend and finished near intraday highs, reflecting emerging momentum in metals and mining.

sectors.name: Oil & Energy (USO / RSPG)
sectors.action: Crude oil proxy USO recorded a 1.8% daily drop, marking its third consecutive weekly decline. The equal-weighted energy ETF (RSPG) rallied over two sessions to test its 50-day moving average line as potential overhead resistance.

stocks.action: Advanced 4.5% on heavy volume, breaking out of a consolidation pattern. It displayed a "blue dot" on its chart, signifying that its relative strength (RS) line achieved a new high at the point of breakout.
Surged 10% on Friday following a 6% upside reversal on Thursday, putting the metal products stock up nearly 18% for the week.

The Japanese semiconductor equipment provider (a $100B+ market cap ADR) jumped 8.4% on a strong breakout with an RS line blue dot. Its gappy price action reflects overnight trading adjustments on foreign exchanges.

strategy.title: Position Sizing & Risk Management
strategy.text: For traders holding cash, analysts advise incremental purchases rather than aggressive all-in allocations. Starting with smaller position sizes allows wider stop-loss margins without taking excessive portfolio risk, permitting traders to add capital as individual positions confirm strength.

strategy.title: Weekend Preparation
strategy.text: Investors are encouraged to update watchlists, monitor sector-level breadth (such as equal-weight tech ETF RSPT), set automated price alerts at key technical levels, and clearly map out both bullish and bearish inflection rules to avoid emotional decision-making during market hours.

strategy.title: Navigating Choppy Action
strategy.text: Divided markets frequently lure active traders into false breakouts ("head fakes") before failing, leading to portfolio whipsaws.

strategy.title: Execution Guidelines
